who: Tara M. McCarthy, historian of women, immigration and social reform at Central Michigan University; history PhD, Rochester, 2005.

evidence.says: CMU history faculty profile gives a Rochester history PhD in 2005 and lists Respectability and Reform (2018).
The authority identifies Tara M. McCarthy through Respectability and Reform (2018), describing her as an associate professor of history at Central Michigan University.

notes: Institution, doctorate and publication agree; the Tara M. authority is the historian's record.

who: Stephen Lee McFarland, historian of military aviation and the Middle East at Auburn University; history PhD, Texas, 1981.

evidence.says: His 2006 CV records a Texas history PhD in 1981, a dissertation on the Iranian crises of 1941–1947, and continuous Auburn history appointments from 1981, including professor from 1995.
The Stephen Lee McFarland authority cites his 1981 work The crisis in Iran, 1941–1947.

notes: The dissertation's subject and year identify the LC author; his Auburn appointment covers Berg's 2001 doctorate.

who: Robert E. McGlone, historian of nineteenth-century America, memory and John Brown at the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa; PhD, UCLA.

evidence.says: The department identifies Robert E. McGlone as a Hawaiʻi history professor for 45 years beginning in 1968, gives his UCLA PhD as 1972, and names his book John Brown's War Against Slavery.
The Robert E. McGlone authority cites John Brown's War Against Slavery (2009) and explicitly associates its author with the University of Hawaii.

notes: University and distinctive book establish the match. The department gives PhD 1972, whereas the AHA entry gives 1971.

who: Paul Charles Milazzo, historian of American politics and environmental policy at Ohio University; PhD, Virginia, 2001.

evidence.says: Ohio University's history department identifies Paul Milazzo as its graduate studies director.
The University of Virginia foundation records Milazzo's Virginia PhD in 2001 and research interests in political development, Congress and environmental policy.
The department lists Unlikely Environmentalists: Congress and Clean Water, 1945–1972 (2006) as Paul Milazzo's book.
The Paul Charles Milazzo authority was established from the 2006 environmentalists book.

notes: Doctorate, university and distinctive publication agree.

who: Bethany Moreton, Dartmouth historian of capitalism and twentieth-century America; history PhD, Yale, 2006; co-chair of Hannah Waits's Berkeley dissertation.

evidence.says: The repository's indexed dissertation abstract identifies Hannah R. Waits's Berkeley history doctorate and names Bethany Moreton and Mark Peterson as co-chairs.
Dartmouth identifies Moreton as professor of history, gives her Yale history doctorate in 2006, and lists To Serve God and Wal-Mart (2009).
The Bethany Moreton authority is established from To Serve God and Wal-Mart (2009).

notes: The dissertation directly confirms supervision despite the different faculty institution; doctorate and book connect her to the LC record.

who: Chester M. "Bo" Morgan III, historian at the University of Southern Mississippi; PhD, Memphis.

evidence.says: Eve Wade's 2019 dissertation Becoming Bronzeville names Chester "Bo" Morgan as committee chair.
The graduate catalog lists Chester "Bo" M. Morgan III as professor of history with a Memphis PhD.
USM attributes Redneck Liberal: Theodore G. Bilbo and the New Deal (1985) to Chester M. "Bo" Morgan III.
The Chester M. Morgan authority is established from Redneck Liberal (1985).

notes: Exact student supervision, PhD institution and book establish the match.

who: Lincoln A. Mullen, historian of American religion and digital history at George Mason University; history PhD, Brandeis, 2014.

evidence.says: His faculty page gives the Brandeis history PhD in 2014, appointment at Mason from that year, The Chance of Salvation (2017), and Jannelle Legg's 2021 dissertation among his supervised dissertations.
The Lincoln A. Mullen authority cites The Chance of Salvation (2017) and a Mason faculty page identifying the same institution and American religious and digital history fields.

notes: Exact student supervision and doctorate agree; LC explicitly identifies the Mason historian.

who: Donald Christopher Nugent, historian of the Reformation and religious thought at the University of Kentucky; Iowa PhD, 1965.

evidence.says: The 1989 American Historical Review contribution identifies its author as Donald Christopher Nugent, University of Kentucky.
Iowa's indexed history newsletter identifies Donald Nugent as a 1965 PhD on leave from Kentucky, with a forthcoming book on the Colloquy of Poissy.
This authority identifies Donald Clark Nugent as a federal district judge for the Northern District of Ohio.
This authority identifies Donald G. Nugent through the 1955 publication How Do School Boards Function?, coauthored with B. Hayes.
A 1962 newspaper in the University of North Texas repository identifies Donald G. Nugent as executive secretary of the Texas Association of School Boards.

notes: Neither supplied authority identifies the Kentucky historian: Donald Clark and Donald G. are distinct from Donald Christopher Nugent.
